study.title: Revelation 13 - the two beasts, false worship, and the number of the beast
study.overview: Revelation 13 presents two symbolic figures acting together against God and against the holy people. The first beast arises from the sea with signs of political, military and blasphemous power; it receives authority from the dragon and demands universal admiration. The second beast arises from the earth, acts as a religious and propagandistic agent of the first, performs misleading signs, promotes an image for worship and imposes a mark linked to economic control. The chapter ends with an appeal to wisdom: the number of the beast should be calculated, and the text identifies it as six hundred and sixty-six. The general picture is of organized opposition to God, but also of temporary limitation of evil and called to the perseverance of the saints.

outline.title: The first beast: idolatrous political power
outline.explanation: John sees a beast rising from the sea, with traces of various animals, heads, horns and diadems. The text binds it to the dragon, showing that his power is not neutral, but derived from Satan. The world is amazed, worships the beast and marvels at its apparent invincibility.

outline.title: Blasphemy, persecution and perseverance of the saints
outline.explanation: The beast receives an arrogant mouth to blaspheme against God and authority for forty-two months, a limited time. She makes war against the saints and seems to win, but this victory is only allowed and provisional. Verse 10 recalls that violence and captivity return upon the oppressor itself, and concludes: here is the patience and faith of the saints.

outline.title: The second beast: religious deception and the mark of the beast
outline.explanation: The second beast looks like lamb, but speaks like a dragon, revealing meek appearance and satanic voice. It promotes the worship of the first beast through deceitful signs, living image and coercion. Then impose a mark on the right hand or on the forehead, controls the purchase and sale and closes with the riddle of the number 666, which requires wisdom to be understood.

study.context: The given notes relate the first beast to Roman power and mention that in the first century Roman emperors claimed more and more divinity. Tyndale also notes that the healed wound can allude to Domitius or to the idea of constant reemergence of evil. Matthew Henry and Adam Clarke show that many performers see in the two beasts depictions of Rome in their civil, religious or imperial aspects, although there is a divergence over the details. The biblical text, however, does not require that every historical identification be resolved to capture its main message: evil is organized in power, worship and deception.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that there is a kind of evil trinity: the dragon, the first beast and the second beast. Political power can become idolatrous when it requires admiration that belongs to God; religion can become an instrument of lies when it speaks as a dragon, although it seems lamb. The blasphemies show that the conflict is of everything theological: the beast attacks the name of God, its tabernacle and those that belong to heaven. The authority of the beast is real, but limited and granted for a defined time, which prevents any fatalistic reading. The church is called not triumphalism, but perseverance, faith and patience. The number 666 functions as a symbol of wisdom: evil has human identity and limited, never divine; therefore, it does not deserve worship, but discernment.

scholarViews.insight: The first beast probably represents Roman power, with political and military power, and the dragon as his ultimate source of authority.
The second beast is understood as a great impostor who, under religious appearance and meekness, deceives people and promotes idolatry.
The number 666 is presented as the very symbolic name of the beast, being a riddle that requires careful interpretation.

questions: Where today does political, cultural or religious power ask for a loyalty that rivals worship due to God?
What signs of the appearance of lamb, but dragon's voice, can appear in religious or moral discourses of our time?
How can the promise that evil is limited can strengthen the patience and faith of the saints in the face of pressure and persecution?
study.practice: Read this chapter as a call to discernment. Examine whether there are areas in which you are being seduced by power, fear, consumption or public approval. Reaffirm your fidelity to Christ in concrete decisions: what you worship, what you accept as truth and what you refuse to obey when it contradicts the gospel. Practice perseverance: if the opposition seems strong, remember that the authority of the beast is granted and temporary, while the Lamb remains sovereign.
study.uncertainty: There are real differences between commentators on the historical identification of the beasts and the scope of number 666. The notes provided allow us to safely say that the chapter portrays idolatrous power, religious deception, persecution and a symbolic number of difficult reading, but do not authorize to affirm with absolute certainty which person or specific system John had in mind in every detail.
